title: Article
description: A long-form authored piece — a blog post, news article, or essay. More structured than Note.

name.description: The Article's title — required for an Article (unlike a Note).

content.description: The Article body. Often HTML in fediverse usage.

mediaType.description: MIME type of the content (defaults to text/html in fediverse usage).

tag.description: Tags, hashtags, or mentions attached to the Article.

title: Document
description: A generic document — a self-contained piece of content with a title, body, and metadata. Spans foaf:Document, schema:CreativeWork, and as:Document.

content.description: The Document's body — plain text or HTML.

mediaType.description: MIME type of the content (text/html, text/markdown, application/pdf, …).

attributedTo.description: The Person or Actor who authored the Document.

title: Event
description: A scheduled occurrence with a start (and usually end) time. Aligns with as:Event, schema:Event, and ical:Vevent at the term level.

summary.description: A short summary or description of the Event.

location.description: Where the Event takes place — a Place reference (URI) or a free-text string.

attributedTo.description: The Person or Actor responsible for the Event.

url.description: A canonical web URL for the Event (often distinct from @id for fediverse content).

title: Note
description: A short text post — the fediverse-canonical Note.

content.description: The note text. May contain HTML in fediverse usage.

summary.description: Optional short summary or content warning.

published.description: ISO-8601 datetime the note was published.

updated.description: ISO-8601 datetime of the most recent edit.

attributedTo.description: The author — Person or Actor reference.

inReplyTo.description: Optional reference to the Note this is a reply to.

to.description: Audience the note is addressed to (often urn:solid:Public for public posts).

title: Person
description: A human person — schema for data typed as urn:solid:Person.

@id.description: The Person's identifier (typically a WebID or DID).

@type.description: The type marker. Bare 'Person' or the explicit urn:solid:Person form.

homepage.description: URL of the Person's primary website.

img.description: URL of an image of the Person.

knows.description: Other People this Person knows. Each entry is a WebID URI.

title: Tracker
description: A container for tracking work items — typically a list of iCalendar Vtodos. The list-level counterpart to single-task Vtodo.

modified.description: When the Tracker was most recently updated (ISO 8601).

initialState.description: iCalendar status assigned to newly-created Vtodos in this Tracker (default: NEEDS-ACTION).

issue.description: The Vtodos this Tracker contains. Each entry is a Vtodo (inline) or a reference (string/object @id).

title: VerifiableCredential
description: A W3C Verifiable Credential — a tamper-evident, cryptographically-signed claim made by an issuer about a subject.

@context.description: JSON-LD context. VC requires the credentials v1 or v2 context to be present.

@id.description: The Credential's identifier — often a UUID or HTTPS URL.

@type.description: Must include VerifiableCredential, optionally plus a more specific subtype.

issuer.description: The party that issued the credential. Either an IRI or an Object with @id and optional metadata.

issuanceDate.description: When the credential was issued (ISO 8601). VC 1.x.

validFrom.description: When the credential becomes valid (ISO 8601). VC 2.0 alternative to issuanceDate.

validUntil.description: When the credential ceases to be valid (ISO 8601). VC 2.0 alternative to expirationDate.

credentialSubject.description: The entity the credential makes claims about. Object (one subject) or array (many subjects). Each carries @id and arbitrary claim properties.

credentialStatus.description: Reference to a status mechanism (revocation list, status list).

proof.description: Cryptographic proof — issuer signature. Object (one proof) or array (multiple proofs).

title: Vtodo
description: An iCalendar to-do item — a task with status, priority, and optional due dates. RFC 5545 compatible.

summary.description: The task title — what to do.

duration.description: How long the task is expected to take (xsd:duration, e.g. PT30M).

completed.description: When the task was marked complete (ISO 8601).
